_comment: Drills kept in the repo instead of Notion. Written in our own words from public coaching material, with the source credited. Same record shape as drills.json; the diagram of each drill is in drill-diagrams/<slug>.json.

fields.Name: Centre-line 2 vs 1 with Backcheck
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 2 forwards (Players 1 and 2) facing each other on the centre line, one at each board
  • 1 defender in each half (Player 3 left, Player 4 right)
  • 2 goalies
  • Balls start with Player 1

Sequence

  1. Player 1 plays a cross pass to Player 2.
  2. Player 2 picks a direction and both forwards attack the defender in that half: a 2 vs 1.
  3. The defender in the other half chases straight away and tries to turn the 2 vs 1 into a 2 vs 2.
  4. Player 2 draws the defender and passes across; Player 1 finishes directly.

Coaching Points

  • Attack fast: every extra pass gives the backchecking defender time to arrive.
  • The backchecking defender starts at the moment of the cross pass, not when the attack is already on.
  • The defender in front stays between ball and goal and delays the attack.

Variations

  • Forwards and defenders pass the ball around freely until the coach calls the start.
  • Let the attack start from both sides, so the forwards cannot plan the direction.

fields.Name: Attack from the Goalie Throw
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 3 players + 2 goalies, full rink
  • Balls start with the goalie of the defending end
  • Player 1 near the own goal, Player 2 high on the same side, Player 3 at the far board in the attacking half

Sequence

  1. Player 1 comes towards the goalie and receives the throw.
  2. Player 1 passes Player 2 into the run along the board.
  3. Player 2 carries the ball and plays a long diagonal pass to Player 3, who runs along the far board towards the centre.
  4. Players 1 and 2 move into shooting positions in the meantime: Player 1 into the slot, Player 2 to the far post.
  5. Player 3 passes to one of them, who shoots directly.

Coaching Points

  • Every pass has to be precise, otherwise the timing breaks.
  • Players 1 and 2 stand offset to Player 3, so Player 3 always has two passing lanes.
  • Pass early enough that the shooter can arrive at speed.

Variations

  • Fix the finishing spots: Player 1 to the far post, Player 2 to the middle.
  • Allow Player 3 to finish alone if the lanes are closed.

fields.Name: 1 vs 1 Dribble Square
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • A square of about 8 × 8 m with a cone gate in the middle of each side
  • 2 players per square: Player 1 attacks, Player 2 defends; 1 ball
  • Set up several squares so the whole team plays at once

Sequence

  1. The attacker tries to dribble through one of two opposite gates (here: left or right).
  2. The defender tries to win the ball.
  3. If the defender wins it, the roles flip: the new attacker goes for the other two gates.
  4. Play 5 rounds: who wins more duels?

Coaching Points

  • Fake a dribble towards one gate, then change direction suddenly.
  • Keep the ball close to the blade and away from the defender's stick.
  • Defenders stay on their feet and steer the attacker away from the gates.

Variations

  • Play for 45, 60 or 90 seconds instead of rounds.
  • Move the gates or make them narrower.

fields.Name: Follow-the-Pass Square
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 4 groups standing at the corners of a square (5–8 m per side)
  • 1 ball, starting with the first player of one group

Sequence

  1. The first player passes clockwise to the first player of the next group.
  2. Right after the pass, the passer runs after the ball and joins the back of that group.
  3. The next player in the passer's group steps up, ready for the ball to come round.
  4. The receiver passes on to the next corner and follows the pass in the same way.

Coaching Points

  • Flat, firm passes to the receiver's stick.
  • Move straight after the pass, so there is never a gap at a corner.
  • Receivers show their blade early so the passer has a target.

Variations

  • Make the square bigger or smaller.
  • Forehand only, then backhand only.
  • Change direction, or add a second ball once the group is in rhythm.
  • Finish each round with a shot on goal.

fields.Name: Shot, Breakout and 2 vs 1
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 3 attackers (Players 1, 2, 3) + 1 defender (Player 4) + 2 goalies, full rink
  • Player 1 at the top board with a ball, Player 3 in the low corner with a second ball
  • Player 2 starts in the middle, Player 4 waits in the other half

Sequence

  1. Player 1 passes to Player 2, who comes through the middle and shoots.
  2. Player 2 keeps moving and turns; Player 3 plays the breakout pass into the run.
  3. Players 1 and 2 attack the other goal 2 vs 1 against Player 4.
  4. Player 2 draws the defender and passes; Player 1 finishes.

Coaching Points

  • Shoot directly, then move on at once: the shot is the start of the counter.
  • Do not stand in the passing shadow of the defender.
  • Lots of speed towards the goal in the 2 vs 1.

Variations

  • Player 3 joins the attack: 3 vs 1.
  • A second defender: 3 vs 2.

fields.Name: 2 vs 2 with Outside Passers
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Two goals moved closer together for a small field, 2 goalies
  • 2 vs 2 on the field
  • The other players line up outside in two columns per team; the first of each column is a passing station

Sequence

  1. 2 vs 2 on the small field.
  2. The team on the ball may use its two outside players: 4 vs 2.
  3. An outside player passes straight back into the field.
  4. Only the players on the field can score.
  5. After 45 seconds the coach whistles; the players leave the ball and the next ones play on without a break.

Coaching Points

  • Outside players always know their next option before the ball arrives.
  • Play fast and direct while you have the extra players.
  • A small field means more duels; a bigger one more running and longer passes.

Variations

  • Direct passes only.
  • All outside players may be used: 6 vs 2.
  • Outside players may also shoot.

fields.Name: Streetball 2 vs 2 on One Goal
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • One goal with goalie, one half of the rink
  • 2 vs 2 on the field
  • One column per team at the centre line; the first player of each column is a passing station

Sequence

  1. Both teams play 2 vs 2 on the same goal.
  2. The first player of a column can be used as a station and plays the ball straight back to the team that passed.
  3. When the ball leaves the field, the coach plays in a new one.
  4. After 45 seconds the coach calls the change; the next players take over.

Coaching Points

  • The aim of every attack is a goal: look for the shot early.
  • Use the station to escape pressure, then move into space for the return.

Variations

  • Without stations.
  • With an extra joker.
  • The stations may also shoot.

fields.Name: Goals in the Middle
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Both goals near the centre line, about 2 m away from it, open towards the ends
  • 2 goalies
  • 4 vs 4 (or 5 vs 5) on the whole rink

Sequence

  1. Both teams may score on both goals.
  2. The play keeps changing direction: attack the goal that is free.
  3. Lots of chances from the slot on both sides.

Coaching Points

  • Switch the side quickly; do not crowd one side.
  • The goalies have no defenders behind them: no wild slashing at the goalie.

Variations

  • Change the team size.
  • A joker who always plays with the team on the ball.
  • Goals only from one-timers.
  • Goals only after three passes.
  • Two-second rule: the ball may not be held longer.

fields.Name: Three-Goal Game 4 vs 3
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • One half of the rink: the goal with goalie and two small goals (e.g. vaulting boxes) at the boards near the centre line
  • 4 attackers (red) vs 3 defenders (blue)

Sequence

  1. The four reds attack the goal with the goalie.
  2. When the three blues win the ball, they counter on one of the two small goals at once.
  3. Short shifts, then the next group.

Coaching Points

  • Very fast transition: the first pass after winning the ball decides.
  • Attackers: take the shot before the defence is in place, and be ready to defend the small goals.

Variations

  • Other numbers: 3 vs 2, 3 vs 3, 5 vs 4.
  • Short shifts.

fields.Name: Goal Fight 3 vs 3
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • One goal with goalie
  • 3 vs 3 (or 2 vs 2) right in front of the goal
  • The coach with up to 7 balls; the other players mark the field and keep the balls in

Sequence

  1. The coach plays in a ball: both teams fight for it and try to score on the same goal.
  2. After a goal or a lost ball the coach plays in the next one at once.
  3. One round lasts 20 seconds. Which team scores more?

Coaching Points

  • Look for the shot as fast as possible.
  • Win the duel with the body, then finish.
  • Rebounds: always follow the shot.

Variations

  • Change the size of the field.
  • Uneven numbers.
  • Extra rules, e.g. only direct shots count.

fields.Name: 2 vs 1 in Both Halves
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Full rink, 2 goalies
  • Left half: 2 red attackers and 1 blue defender
  • Right half: 2 blue attackers and 1 red defender
  • Nobody may cross the centre line

Sequence

  1. The two reds attack the left goal 2 vs 1.
  2. Whoever wins the ball (defender or goalie) plays it over the centre line to the own attackers.
  3. Now the two blues attack the right goal 2 vs 1, and so on.

Coaching Points

  • Use the extra player: draw the defender, then pass.
  • Know when to hold the ball and when to play fast.
  • Very intense: plan enough breaks.

Variations

  • 3 vs 2
  • 3 vs 1
  • 2 vs 2
  • 3 vs 3

fields.Name: Joker Game 3 vs 3
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Full rink, 2 goalies
  • 3 vs 3 plus a joker (in a different colour) who plays with the team on the ball
  • The other players wait in two columns per team outside the field

Sequence

  1. 3 vs 3; the joker always joins the team that has the ball: 4 vs 3.
  2. Players and joker may score.
  3. When the ball leaves the field, the coach plays in a new one.
  4. After 45 seconds the coach calls the change; the next three of each column play on without a break.

Coaching Points

  • Use the extra player for fast, direct passing.
  • Every attack aims for a goal: direct, quick, decisive.

Variations

  • 2 vs 2 with goals at both ends.
  • Only direct shots count.
  • Include the outside players.

fields.Name: Keep-Away
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • One half of the rink, no goals
  • Two teams of 2 to 5 players, 1 ball

Sequence

  1. The team on the ball tries to string together as many passes as possible.
  2. The other team tries to touch or intercept the ball.
  3. When the ball is lost, the tasks change.

Coaching Points

  • Little space means pressure: look up before the ball arrives.
  • Defenders aim to intercept passes, not to win the ball in a 1 vs 1.

Variations

  • Teams of 2, 3, 4 or 5.
  • Make the field smaller or bigger.
  • Direct passes only.

fields.Name: Race to the Ball at the Board
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Pairs side by side, facing the board
  • One ball about 50 cm in front of the board
  • Only after a good warm-up

Sequence

  1. On the whistle both players sprint to the ball.
  2. The first one puts a foot on the ball and holds it for a few seconds without losing balance.
  3. Only the body may be used, with the shoulder charges allowed in the game.

Coaching Points

  • Correct body contact: no arms, no legs.
  • Quick first steps, low centre of gravity.

Variations

  • With or without sticks.
  • Start with the back to the ball; the coach may move the ball before the whistle.

fields.Name: Number Passing
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Groups of 3 to 5 players, one ball per group
  • The players get numbers and move freely in their area

Sequence

  1. Number 1 passes to number 2, 2 to 3, and so on; the last one plays back to 1.
  2. Everybody keeps moving the whole time.

Coaching Points

  • Know where the next receiver is before the ball arrives.
  • Flat, accurate passes.

Variations

  • Change the group size.
  • Make the area smaller.
  • Carry the ball for at most 3 seconds.
  • Direct passes only.
  • Several balls per group.

fields.Name: Ego Game
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • A normal game on one or two goals, e.g. 3 vs 3
  • Passing is not allowed

Sequence

  1. The player on the ball may never pass.
  2. The only way to hand over the ball: leave it standing for a team-mate who crosses behind.
  3. The defenders put the ball carrier under pressure with two or even three players.

Coaching Points

  • Protect the ball with the body; keep it close to the blade.
  • Team-mates cross close behind to take over the ball.
  • Coaches: encourage players who lose the ball.

Variations

  • The ball may not be handed over at all.

fields.Name: Pass and Duel
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Pairs with one ball, moving freely in the hall

Sequence

  1. The two players move and pass to each other.
  2. On the whistle they play a 1 vs 1 in a small space.
  3. 30–40 seconds of passing, then 10 seconds of duel, alternating, for 6–10 minutes in all.

Coaching Points

  • Very intense interval training.
  • Switch from partner to opponent in a split second.

Variations

  • Change the rhythm (passing vs. duel).
  • Define the space for the duel.

fields.Name: Fruit Salad
fields.Source: mobilesport.ch (BASPO / swiss unihockey), Unihockey spielend entdecken 12/2013
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Four groups in the four corners of the hall
  • Every child dribbles a ball
  • Each group picks a fruit name

Sequence

  1. The coach calls two fruits: those two groups swap corners as fast as possible, ball on the stick.
  2. On "Fruit salad!" all groups swap corners diagonally.

Coaching Points

  • Keep the ball close to the blade.
  • Look up when crossing the other groups.

Variations

  • Animal names instead of fruits; the children imitate the animal.
  • Walk instead of run: on tiptoes, crouched, on one leg.
  • Obstacles in the hall.
  • Swap the ball with another child when crossing.

fields.Name: Newspaper Reader
fields.Source: mobilesport.ch (BASPO / swiss unihockey), Unihockey spielend entdecken 12/2013
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • One child (the "reader") stands with the back to the group, facing a wall
  • All other children with a ball at the start line

Sequence

  1. All children dribble towards the reader.
  2. The reader calls "one, two, stop!" and turns round.
  3. Everybody has to stop the ball at once. Whoever still moves goes back to the start.
  4. Who gets closest to the reader?

Coaching Points

  • Control the ball with the stick, eyes up.
  • Fast and slow: change the speed all the time.

Variations

  • Without the call.
  • The ball may be stopped with the hand or the foot.

fields.Name: Passing Stations
fields.Source: mobilesport.ch (BASPO / swiss unihockey), Unihockey spielend entdecken 12/2013
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Two groups
  • Group 1: each child stands in a hoop somewhere on the field (the stations)
  • Group 2: each child dribbles a ball across the hall

Sequence

  1. The dribblers move freely through the hall.
  2. At any station they play a one-two and dribble on with the ball.
  3. Swap the groups after a while.

Coaching Points

  • Pass to the blade of the station, move on straight away.
  • Stations: ready all the time, play the ball straight back.

Variations

  • Forehand and backhand passes.
  • Competition: who plays the most one-twos in a given time?

fields.Name: Star Passing
fields.Source: mobilesport.ch (BASPO / swiss unihockey), Unihockey spielend entdecken 12/2013
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Small groups of 4–6 children in a circle
  • One child in the middle with a ball

Sequence

  1. The child in the middle passes to the outside players in turn.
  2. Each outside player plays the ball straight back.
  3. Change the player in the middle after a round.

Coaching Points

  • Flat passes to the blade.
  • The middle player turns the body towards each receiver.

Variations

  • The middle player chooses the order.
  • Competition between groups.
  • Direct passes only, no control.
  • Change direction on the whistle.

fields.Name: Dribble Round the Cone and Shoot
fields.Source: mobilesport.ch (BASPO / swiss unihockey), Unihockey spielend entdecken 12/2013
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • One goal with goalie
  • A cone in front of the goal
  • The children in a line, each with a ball

Sequence

  1. The first child dribbles round the cone.
  2. Then it shoots on goal.
  3. The next child starts as soon as the first has shot.

Coaching Points

  • Keep the ball close in the turn round the cone.
  • Look at the goal before the shot.

Variations

  • A slalom instead of one cone.
  • Touch the cone with the hand.
  • Cones in different colours: the coach calls which one.
  • A child without stick stands at the cone instead (passive defender).

fields.Name: Knock Down the Cones
fields.Source: mobilesport.ch (BASPO / swiss unihockey), Unihockey spielend entdecken 12/2013
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Every child puts up a cone (or club) somewhere in the hall
  • 3–4 balls for the whole group

Sequence

  1. Everybody protects their own cone and tries to knock down the others with a shot.
  2. Only hits with the ball count.
  3. Whose cone is hit does an extra task, puts the cone up again and plays on.

Coaching Points

  • Short, accurate shots beat hard ones.
  • Keep an eye on your own cone while you attack.

Variations

  • Play in teams.

fields.Name: Pass Behind the Goal into 2 vs 1
fields.Source: David Malkus, bachelor thesis on attacking combinations for juniors, University of West Bohemia (Plzeň), 2021
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Players in both corners behind the goal and at the board on the centre line, the same number at each station
  • Goalie
  • Balls start in one corner

Sequence

  1. The player in the corner passes behind the goal to the other corner and runs in front of the goal.
  2. The receiver plays the ball up the board to the centre line and becomes the defender.
  3. The third player starts a 2 vs 1 with the player in front of the goal.
  4. The player in front of the goal times the move into free space for the pass and finishes fast.

Coaching Points

  • A basic combination for every session: pass and go.
  • Time the move away from the defender, do not wait standing.

Variations

  • Rotate the stations after every round.
  • Allow the defender to start earlier.

fields.Name: 2 vs 1 after a Wall Pass
fields.Source: David Malkus, bachelor thesis on attacking combinations for juniors, University of West Bohemia (Plzeň), 2021
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • 3 attackers + 1 defender + goalie
  • Player 2 in the middle with the ball, Players 1 and 3 at the boards

Sequence

  1. Player 2 plays the ball to the defender and gets it straight back.
  2. Player 2 passes to one of the two others.
  3. Players 1 and 3 attack the goal 2 vs 1.

Coaching Points

  • The ball carrier reads the defender: pass or shoot yourself?
  • Attack with speed, keep the width.

Variations

  • Player 2 joins as a third attacker: 3 vs 1.

fields.Name: 3 vs 2 into 2 vs 1
fields.Source: David Malkus, bachelor thesis on attacking combinations for juniors, University of West Bohemia (Plzeň), 2021
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Full rink, 2 goalies
  • 3 blue attackers, 2 red defenders

Sequence

  1. The blues attack 3 vs 2 and finish with a shot.
  2. The goalie throws the ball to the two reds, who now attack.
  3. The blue closest to the own goal becomes the defender: 2 vs 1 towards the other goal.

Coaching Points

  • Typical for overtime: fast counters after every shot.
  • Switch from attack to defence the moment the shot is taken.

Variations

  • The second blue may backcheck: 2 vs 2.

fields.Name: Round the Goal: 2 vs 1, then 3 vs 2
fields.Source: David Malkus, bachelor thesis on attacking combinations for juniors, University of West Bohemia (Plzeň), 2021
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Full rink, 2 goalies
  • 2 attackers at their own goal, 1 defender at the other end
  • 2 more defenders wait behind the boards

Sequence

  1. The attackers run round their own goal; the goalie throws in the ball.
  2. 2 vs 1 towards the other goal.
  3. After the finish everybody runs round that goal, and the defender joins the attackers.
  4. Now 3 vs 2 against the two defenders who waited behind the boards.

Coaching Points

  • Play at top speed.
  • Room for creativity: crossing, screens, give and go.

fields.Name: 2 vs 2 after a Lost Ball
fields.Source: David Malkus, bachelor thesis on attacking combinations for juniors, University of West Bohemia (Plzeň), 2021
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • One half, goalie
  • 2 defenders (blue), 2 attackers (red); one attacker waits in the corner of the defenders' end

Sequence

  1. A defender at the centre line passes into his own corner.
  2. The attacker there wins the ball.
  3. He plays behind the goal to his team-mate.
  4. 2 vs 2: the defenders must reorganise at once.

Coaching Points

  • Simulates a turnover in the own half: react immediately.
  • Attacker without the ball: get free and finish fast.

fields.Name: Point Shot, then Overload
fields.Source: David Malkus, bachelor thesis on attacking combinations for juniors, University of West Bohemia (Plzeň), 2021
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • One half (can run on both halves at the same time), goalie
  • Queues at every position: corner, point, centre line, diagonal corner

Sequence

  1. The corner player passes to the defender at the point, who shoots at once.
  2. At the same moment a player with a ball starts from the centre line together with the player in the diagonal corner.
  3. They attack 2 vs 1 against the shooter, who switches to defence.

Coaching Points

  • Good with many players: queues give a quick follow-up.
  • Point shot low and hard, for tips and rebounds.

fields.Name: 3 vs 1 with a Drop Pass
fields.Source: David Malkus, bachelor thesis on attacking combinations for juniors, University of West Bohemia (Plzeň), 2021
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • One half, goalie
  • 3 attackers at the centre line, 1 defender with the ball

Sequence

  1. The defender starts with a pass to one of the attackers.
  2. The attacker passes to a team-mate, who carries the ball backwards.
  3. This gives the defender time to drop back, but the attackers can fill the lanes.
  4. 3 vs 1 to a finish.

Coaching Points

  • Hold the ball until the support arrives: more options, better chance.
  • The attackers fill the width and the slot.

fields.Name: 1 vs 1, 2 vs 2, 3 vs 3 Escalation
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • One half, goalie
  • Two teams of three, numbered 1 to 3

Sequence

  1. 20 seconds 1 vs 1.
  2. Whistle: the second pair joins, 2 vs 2 for 20 seconds.
  3. Whistle: the third pair joins, 3 vs 3.
  4. Next round, players number 2 start with the 1 vs 1, and so on.

Coaching Points

  • Ball carrier: solve the 1 vs 1 with fakes.
  • Without the ball: win your duel and get free; always active.

fields.Name: Top Scorer
fields.Page Content:
Setup

  • Small goals spread over the field
  • Half as many balls as children

Sequence

  1. Every child may score on every goal.
  2. Who has no ball tries to win one.
  3. Who scores the most goals?

Coaching Points

  • Look for the 1 vs 1 bravely.
  • Shortest way to the goal.
